extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator; educated 18th-century literate public interested in manners, literature, and social conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Short periodical essay offering commentary and normative judgments about personal conduct, marriage, literary precedence, and public manners aimed at a coffeehouse/urban literate audience. The piece mixes moral instruction, social observation, and literary anecdote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugal love as a superior refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: If Love be any Refinement, Conjugal Love must be certainly so in a much higher Degree. The passion of love to a mistress resembles too much the Flame of a Fever; that to a Wife is like the Vital Heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conjugal love is praised as a deeper, more durable refinement: a regular and uniform endeavour to make yourself valuable both as friend and lover, cultivating the mind and improving behaviour. It is the parent of substantial virtues and agreeable qualities, as opposed to the frivolous affectations of amorous gallantry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style and substance of letters to wives vs mistresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters written by Men of Goodnature to their Wives, notwithstanding any Inequality of Style, would appear to have the Advantage. Friendship, Tenderness and Constancy, drest in a Simplicity of Expression, recommend themselves by a more native Elegance than passionate Raptures, extravagant Encomiums, and slavish Adoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When addressing a wife, prefer simplicity, expressions of friendship, tenderness, and constancy over overwrought passion and flattery. Such plainness recommends itself by a natural elegance and better reflects lasting affection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of the exemplary husband (Benevolus model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Benevolus, both in Publick and Private, on all Occasions of Life, appears to have every good Quality and desirable Ornament. Abroad he is reverenced and esteemed; at home beloved and happy. The Satisfaction he enjoys there, settles into an habitual Complacency, which shines in his Countenance, enlivens his Wit, and seasons his Conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exemplary husband combines public respectability with domestic affection: his contentment at home produces a visible composure that improves his wit and social intercourse. Such a man is a steadfast friend and agreeable companion; domestic happiness ennobles public character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of proper ideas; avoid satirical denigration of marriage and good-nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Many Writings under the Notion of Humour have made 'Good-Nature' suspicious and transferred it from its original Sense to that of 'Folly'. The writer's ambition is to restore the proper Ideas of things, particularly on the Subject of Marriage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical and humorous writing should not systematically deride marriage, sobriety, or good-nature. The author urges correcting prevalent literary fashions that make virtue a target of satire; evaluate works by whether they distort or restore proper social/ethical ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-manners observational checklist (deputation instructions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe behaviour of all persons and things conveyed in coaches, carried in carts, or walking on foot between London and Westminster; note whether married couples appear pleased or tired with each other; whether persons preserve their former countenance after an Addition of Honour or Riches; whether persons on foot are dress'd suitable to their condition; distinguish such as appear discreet by a low-heel Shoe with a Leather-Garter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deputed observer is to record specific signs of propriety or affectation: carriage behaviour of couples, changes in demeanour after gaining honour/wealth, suitable dress for social station (low-heel shoe, leather garter as signals of discretion), ostentatious strutting and swearing, coach-box affectations among young gentlemen, and similar public indicators of virtue or folly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties and procedural constraints of the public observer
rubrics_metrics.description: You are authorized and depute from the hours of Nine in the Morning, till Four in the Afternoon, to keep a strict Eye ... You are therefore not to depart from your Observatory at the end of Devereux-Court during the said space of each Day ... and give Advertisement thereof to me at all convenient and spectatorial Hours ... Hereof you are not to fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The observer is given concrete working hours and a fixed post; duty requires continuous presence during specified times, careful reporting of observations to the editor, and attention to secret supplementary articles. This establishes procedural expectations for moral/sociological surveillance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedence among authors determined by format/edition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Author of a Folio, in all Companies and Conversations, sets himself above the Author of a Quarto; the Author of a Quarto above the Author of an Octavo; and so on, by a gradual Descent and Subordination, to an Author in Twenty Fours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literary rank and social precedence are culturally assigned according to the physical format/size and edition of an author's works (folio > quarto > octavo > duodecimo > twenty-fours). Authors and their printers/booksellers are expected to observe this ceremonial hierarchy in assemblies and seating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedence among theatrical professions and poetic genres
rubrics_metrics.description: A Tragedian always takes place of a Comedian; merry Drolls who make us laugh are always placed at the lower End of the Table. By parity of reason, all Writers of Tragedy look upon it as their due to be seated, served, or saluted before Comick Writers; those who deal in Tragi-Comedy usually take their Seats between the Authors of either Side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage and genre hierarchies are socially enforced: tragedians and serious/heroic poets rank above comedians and burlesque writers; tragi-comedians occupy middle ground. These conventions determine seating, salutation, and deference in learned and theatrical circles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of bachelor libertinism and civic duty to marry
rubrics_metrics.description: The Case of Celibacy is the great Evil of our Nation ... Augustus ... told the Batchelors that their Lives and Actions had been so peculiar, that he knew not by what Name to call 'em ... That their Course of Life was of such pernicious Consequence to the Glory and Grandeur of the Roman Nation ... they were guilty of Murder, in not suffering those to be born which should proceed from them ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay treats marriage as a civic duty: social health is measured by births, marriages, and burials. It advocates scrutiny of bachelorhood as a public ill and suggests that state incentives or penalties (distinguishing bachelors to their disadvantage) could be considered to correct societal decay caused by libertine single men.
